rows.claim: `.ufo/evidence/round-14/verification-final.json` retains the corrected selftest and frozen before/after outcomes
rows.excerpt: "supersedes": "verification.json disposition_selftest failure only; original real before/after observations remain valid"
rows.note: Path pointer, whole file at base (git show 8ca67421111fa354b47b803358391d0b07fc6db9:.ufo/evidence/round-14/verification-final.json). The file carries checks[0] disposition_selftest exit 0 expected 0 (the corrected selftest, against verification.json's exit 1 expected 0 for the same check) plus checks[1] unresolved_before exit 1 expected 1 and checks[2] resolved_after exit 0 expected 0 with their full stdout (frozen before/after outcomes), and measured_commit 64314783836bb0d05ad06a774d7310fd3a23b5bd with a 6-entry input_sha256 map; supersedes is the top-level field quoted. The section's next sentence ("The revision measured is recorded separately") matches measured_commit in the same file. Lines did not drift (path pointer).

rows.heading: ## Effective expectation reconciliation — round 14
rows.claim: `verification.json` retains the initial18-of34 fixture failures rather than disguising them as green
rows.excerpt: SELFTEST_CASE clean-superseded FAIL (exit=1 expects=0; ids=['expected_contains_missing'] expects=[]; payload exit=1; status='failed' expects='clean')
rows.note: Bare basename: resolve() (measure.py:188-192) tries verification.json, corpus/knowledge/, corpus/ and corpus/lessons/ and finds no blob, so check_reads (measure.py:270-279) can only score this pointer unresolved; the file the sentence means is held at .ufo/evidence/round-14/verification.json (78 lines at base). Its content is sound: checks[0] disposition_selftest exit 1 expected 0 and `git show 8ca67421111fa354b47b803358391d0b07fc6db9:.ufo/evidence/round-14/verification.json | grep -o "SELFTEST_CASE [^ ]* \(PASS\|FAIL\)"` gives 34 case lines of which 18 are FAIL — the sentence's 18-of-34. tools/evidence-disposition.py:181 says "`--selftest` builds isolated /tmp fixtures", so "fixture failures" is the right noun. Only the pointer form is wrong, not the fact. Observed rendering artifact, left alone: the sentence reads initial18-of34 (no space).

proposed_fix.fixed_excerpt: SELFTEST_CASE clean-superseded FAIL (exit=1 expects=0; ids=['expected_contains_missing'] expects=[]; payload exit=1; status='failed' expects='clean')
proposed_fix.why: The pointer keeps its name but gains the directory it lives in, so it resolves to a held blob and the 18-of-34 FAIL lines quoted are inside the pointed text; the section keeps its 10 pointers because the bare token stops matching PATH_RE once it is preceded by "/".

rows.heading: ## Effective expectation reconciliation — round 14
rows.claim: the round14 `capture-context.py` produced the retained context receipt and must not be run again because its historical output path replaces that frozen receipt
rows.excerpt: Output: .ufo/evidence/round-14/context-receipt.json (atomic, 0644); no other path is written.
rows.note: Bare basename: resolve() finds no capture-context.py at the lane root, corpus/knowledge/, corpus/ or corpus/lessons/, so the pointer is file-null and unresolved. The file the sentence means is held at .ufo/evidence/round-14/capture-context.py (647 lines at base): its docstring says the one output is .ufo/evidence/round-14/context-receipt.json (atomic, 0644) and OUTPUT_REL at :58 is the same path, which is exactly why re-running it would overwrite the frozen receipt; .ufo/evidence/round-14/verification.json checks[3] context_capture records the retained run (CONTEXT: OK receipt=.ufo/evidence/round-14/context-receipt.json exit=0). The round-14 registry row in the next subsection (SKILL.md:1602) already uses the qualified form, and :1623 uses it again.

proposed_fix.skill_old:
the round14

proposed_fix.fixed_excerpt: Output: .ufo/evidence/round-14/context-receipt.json (atomic, 0644); no other path is written.
proposed_fix.why: The qualified path resolves to the held blob and states the single output path the sentence says a re-run would replace; dropping the now-redundant "the round14 " keeps the clause and the pointer count at 10 (the bare token stops matching once preceded by "/").
